LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 5.3.1 FICTION: PLAY FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why should one read a play?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 5.3.1 Fiction: Play from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group discussion making and actively

participates to discuss the relationships among the characters in the play.

● Learning to learn: This is promoted as the learner independently identifies characters, themes, language and stylistic

devices used in the play.

Values:
● Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates the opinions of others during group discussions.

● Patriotism: This is enhanced as the learner displays awareness of their own responsibilities in the society when relating

characters in the play to real life.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner embraces leadership and good governance skills as they discuss thematic

concerns in the play.
